findings.title: Next.js 14.2.35 is EOL and ships unpatched known CVEs
evidence: docs/release-readiness.md:42 requires CI gate; no dependency gate
findings.impact: Next.js 14 left Maintenance LTS on 2025-10-26 and receives no security fixes; the release artifact embeds the .next build. The deterministic CVEs (CVE-2026-44573 middleware/i18n bypass, CVE-2026-64641 Server Action DoS, CVE-2026-64645 SSRF in rewrites() etc.) affect 14.x and are fixed only in 15.5.x/16.3.x. Real exploitability is low because the app uses the App Router with no middleware, i18n, API routes/use server, dynamic rewrites/redirects, and images are unoptimized; the risk is the permanently unpatched EOL line.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a supported line (15.5.26+ or 16.3.6+); if deferred, record a dated risk acceptance and re-check advisories monthly.

findings.title: Vulnerable transitive copies: nanoid 3.3.15 and nested postcss 8.4.31
findings.impact: nanoid 3.3.15 is below the CVE-2026-67213/67214 fixes (3.3.18/3.3.16): infinite-loop DoS on size 0/negative. Top-level postcss 8.5.15 is patched for CVE-2026-45623 (8.5.12) and CVE-2026-41305 (8.5.10) but still vulnerable to CVE-2026-73646 (8.5.18) and CVE-2026-69153 (8.5.19). The production copy next/node_modules/postcss 8.4.31 is vulnerable to all of these including arbitrary file read via sourceMappingURL. Build-time reachability only; not reached by the shipped client in normal use.
findings.recommendation: Bump the direct postcss dev dep to >=8.5.19 and nanoid to a fixed 3.3.x; defer the Next.js-pinned nested postcss to the framework upgrade in buddy-DEP-001.

findings.title: Release workflow runs install scripts and unpinned actions with a write token
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:13-16 permissions: contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: write
.github/workflows/release.yml:38-39 run: npm ci (executes dependency lifecycle scripts)
findings.impact: All six uses: refs are moving major tags, not 40-hex SHAs. The release job, including npm ci's postinstall scripts, runs with a workflow-scoped token that can write releases (contents: write) and mint OIDC tokens (id-token: write). A compromised dependency or a hijacked third-party action tag (softprops/action-gh-release@v2, attest-build-provenance@v1) inherits that capability and could publish or tamper with releases/attestations.
findings.recommendation: Pin every uses: to a full commit SHA; scope permissions to the job/step that needs writes and keep npm ci under contents: read; prefer npm ci --ignore-scripts or isolate install in a read-only job; bump stale majors (checkout/setup-node v4->v7, attest-build-provenance v1->v4, action-gh-release v2->v3).

findings.title: No dependency-vulnerability, license, or secret-scanning gate in CI
evidence: package.json:17 "audit": "npm audit --omit=dev" (never invoked by a workflow)
package.json:18 "sbom": "npm sbom --sbom-format cyclonedx --omit=dev" (not invoked by CI)
.github/dependabot.yml:2-35 opens update PRs but does not block vulnerable merges
findings.impact: The CI gate proves correctness but does not detect vulnerable dependencies, license obligations, or secret leakage, which is why the DET-P1/2/3 dependencies reached master. Detection (not cure) gap.
findings.recommendation: Add CI jobs: npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev, actions/dependency-review-action on PRs, a gitleaks/secret scan, and a license allow/deny check once a policy exists.

findings.title: Release is not gated by environment protection or protected tags
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:13-16 workflow-scoped write permissions, no needs/approval gate
docs/release-readiness.md:42 condition requires 'protection enabled'; no repo artifact records branch protection
findings.impact: Publishing a v* tag immediately runs the release and publishes a GitHub Release with contents: write. There is no GitHub Environment with required reviewers, no protected-tag rule, and no in-repo evidence of required status checks / branch protection; a maintainer or a stolen write token can tag an unmerged commit. Branch protection is not stored in the repository and was not verifiable from the clone.
findings.recommendation: Create a release GitHub Environment with required reviewers, apply a v* tag protection rule, and enable branch protection on master requiring the CI check and CODEOWNERS review; document in docs/release-process.md.

findings.title: Release SBOM includes dev dependencies, inconsistent with the npm script
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:85,99 SBOM packed and published with the release
findings.impact: The released SBOM describes the full tree including dev dependencies while the documented script describes production only. SBOM consumers cannot tell which set is authoritative, and dev-only CVEs (e.g. nanoid) are mis-attributed to the shipped artifact.
findings.recommendation: Use one SBOM definition; if the release ships production code, generate npm sbom --omit=dev and state excluded items explicitly.

findings.title: .gitattributes missing (no line-ending policy)
evidence: .gitattributes is absent at the repo root (git ls-files returns no .gitattributes)
.github/workflows/ci.yml:21 runs-on: ubuntu-latest (Linux CI) with a Windows dev environment
findings.impact: Without a normalization policy, checkouts differ between Windows (CRLF) and Linux (LF), causing churn and potentially breaking shell-sensitive tooling.
findings.recommendation: Add .gitattributes with '* text=auto eol=lf' and mark binary asset types as binary.

findings.title: Product docs still claim saves are not runtime-validated
evidence: docs/README.md:61 Save validation ... DATA-P1-002 / SEC-P2-001 no runtime save validation ... open (tracked)
lib/storage/schema.ts:177 export function validateSave(input: unknown): SaveValidationResult
lib/storage/indexeddb.ts:3,50,96 imports and calls validateSave on load and import
findings.impact: The code now validates and migrates saves with zod, bounded numbers and a MAX_IMPORT_LENGTH size cap, but the README and reconciled audit matrix still mark the gap open. Generated status artifacts contradict their source of truth, so reviewers/AI agents may re-implement an existing control or mis-state release risk.
findings.recommendation: Update README.md:19-22 and the docs/README.md status matrix to verified-fixed with commit evidence.

findings.title: License is explicitly pending and vendored prompt-pack provenance is unconfirmed
evidence: README.md:118-121 'No license has been chosen yet. Absent an explicit license grant, all rights are reserved'
docs/README.md:28-35 vendored prompt pack authorship/ownership and licensing 'unconfirmed'
findings.impact: The repository is all-rights-reserved by default and a large vendored prompt pack has unconfirmed authorship/licensing, leaving distribution/derivative rights undefined and an unvetted third-party-content supply-chain item.
findings.recommendation: Choose a license (or keep proprietary + internal-only) and record the prompt-pack provenance/ownership decision in NOTICE; add a license-policy gate if the project opens up.
